brief: BofA's Hartnett argues a 2020s regime of fiscal excess and deglobalization is producing an inflationary boom: US nominal GDP is up 63% over six years while 30-year Treasury prices are down 60%, so investors stay long stocks and short bonds until yields hurt growth. Since Fed governor Warsh turned hawkish at Jackson Hole, the 10-year yield is up 60bps and a global tightening cycle (60 hikes YTD vs 20 in 2025) is underway, yet Mag7 broke to new highs after last week's hike. BofA warns a MOVE Index spike plus IXG below $125, or an Iran deal dropping oil $10 while yields keep rising, would trigger risk-off deleveraging; it argues policymaker panic to cap yields has begun and recommends nibbling bonds now (10-22% projected returns if yields fall 100bps). Weekly flows rotated into bonds/cash/gold and out of stocks even as 2026 equity inflows stay record-paced, and the Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 9.3 (Sell) on stretched long-stocks-short-bonds positioning. Base case: yield spikes are the fastest way to end the boom, so BofA favors commodities, EM, growth over cyclicals, and 'peak yield' trades into the midterms, framing Trump as wanting China's low yields, not Xi's stock market.
